This project aims to create a simple yet engaging Tic-Tac-Toe game using C++ for my Computer Graphics & Image Processing course. The primary objective was to implement graphical elements and user interaction, which are crucial aspects of computer graphics. The game features a graphical interface where the player can compete against a computer opponent in a 3x3 grid. Throughout the development process,
applied various concepts learned in the course, such as handling graphical rendering, managing user inputs, and creating basic AI logic.
Develop a visually appealing and functional interface for the game using the graphics.h library.
Implement an AI opponent that can play against the player with basic decision-making capabilities.
Enable players to make moves using mouse clicks and provide feedback based on these inputs.
Create a structured game flow with win/lose conditions and an AI capable of making intelligent moves.

The game starts with a welcome screen displaying the game title and a brief introduction. The interface is designed to be straightforward, with clear instructions and options for the player to choose their symbol ('X' or 'O').

The game continuously checks for a winning condition (three consecutive marks in a row, column, or diagonal) or a draw (no empty cells left).
After the game ends, the player can choose to restart the game or exit. These options are made available through a graphical menu.
This function initializes the graphical interface, sets up the title screen, and displays the game name with some visual effects to create a welcoming atmosphere.
These functions capture mouse clicks and determine whether the player wants to restart or exit the game. It ensures that the player's input is accurately registered and processed.

The playerMove function handles the player's move, while the AI function determines the computer's move using basic decision-making rules. The AI tries to either block the player from winning or take the winning move when available.
This function checks if there is a winning combination on the board. It is called after every move to determine if the game has ended in a win, loss, or draw.
